svg.title: Expected saving versus no skill
svg.desc: Expected targets for the saving versus using no skill at all, net of the skill's own cost; these are not results. Real data today (estimates from runs on sample inputs, no agent runs; negative means the skill costs more than it saves): Documents (HTML only) 57% to 70%; Images −21% to 32%; Plain text, JSON, CSV −64% to 74%; Command output −37% to 99%; Code exploration −94% to 98%; Change review 30% to 88%; Documentation lookup 61% to 90%; Lockfiles and generated 81% to 99%; Fixed context −31% to 42%. Bars are targets. Basis: Documents: target for styled HTML, PDF and Word; Images: ceiling from pixels / 750: 1024 px against the 1568 px API cap; Plain text, JSON, CSV: earlier small samples: JSON compaction 51%, tables 77%; Command output: earlier small samples: filtered log 93%, test summary about 99% (578 tokens against about 44,600); Lockfiles and generated: target: a summary of a few dozen packages instead of tens of thousands of tokens; Code exploration: target: a summary of a few dozen lines instead of reading the files; Change review: earlier sample: a case file about 93% smaller than the diff of three commits; Documentation lookup: earlier sample: a query answers in about 116 tokens and warns that opening the diagram costs about 221; Fixed context: target: trimming what is over the limits. Real data: benchmark counterfactual (inputs read with and without the skill) with inferred token counts (characters / 4, pixels / 750), from runs on sample inputs, the skill's own cost charged in full to every case, values rounded down.
